replies.content: A closure would have been a return to the orphanage, to the uncertainty and the lack of purpose that had always haunted me. It would have meant the loss of the very environment that nurtured my ambition. I had no intention of surrendering to that fate.

I had spoken to Professor Dippet beforehand, assuring him that the matter would be settled before I confronted Hagrid. The faculty would accept the accusation against Hagrid and Aragog without demanding hard proof, so the resolution seemed inevitable. If that had failed, Hogwarts would have closed, forcing me back to the orphanage. My certainty was therefore not about Aragog at all; it was about preserving the school—and my place within it—before the possibility of returning to that bleak, uncertain life.
